assumptions: W8 of PLAN-0006, the last item and the plan's release gate, built in-session by a single writer. It is a CONFORMANCE HARNESS (.warp/tracker_conformance.py) that COMPOSES the shipped pieces (WARP-0601 routing, WARP-0603 seam + FakeTracker, WARP-0604/0607 intake, WARP-0605/0606 mirror) into one end-to-end journey and asserts the invariants; it adds no new capability behavior (C3), proven by a call-count probe that it calls the real sibling functions. It owns regression journeys RJ1 (the conformance is real and FAILS by name on a broken mapping) and RJ2 (the tracker never writes a definition; the repository stays the single source of truth). No template twin (not a validate/policy_check load dependency). A REVIEW-DRIVEN test-strength fix was applied to the reviewed code and re-reviewed: the AC5 capability-honesty assertion now BINDS each capability name to its status via a per-line regex (the prior loose substring check would have rubber-stamped a live adapter mislabeled mechanical) and adds tracker_conformance to the checked set; the offline-conformance boundary (the self-referential shipped-status check, correct by design per C5) was documented in the spec Notes. Two independent adversarial reviews (the full pass on 3824944 and a scoped re-review bound to this commit f753c72) both PASS with 0 blocking; the full review could NOT make the conformance rubber-stamp a broken mapping (RJ1) or slip a repository write-back past it (RJ2).

The offline conformance proves the behavior the vendor-neutral seam owns (routing, the mirror transitions + closing comment, idempotent replay, the one-way guarantee); validating that a mapped status name exists in a live project is the reference-wired adapter's job, not the offline conformance (C5). The two accepted minor notes from the full review (an unreachable defensive branch behind the IntakeError raise; a subset-guard that fires only for a rogue adapter) were left as-is - a defensive branch and a correct subset-guard, not defects.
